label: Game B
nuance_found: Where to put which sandwich tower (cannon splash vs mustard slow vs ballista speed), stacking three different layers for a Club bonus, aim modes, calling waves early for bonus crumbs, and the timed FLAME / RINSE buttons: lighting a burner when a pack of olives walks over it gave a x65 combo and hundreds of crumbs, which changed when I spent and when I tapped.
audio: Cheerful looping stage music that swaps to a driving boss track and a victory jingle, plus splurts, cannon thumps, pops, a placing sound and rising combo chimes on every kill.
furthest_progress: Cleared The Cutting Board (3 stars, 12,500) and The Stovetop including the boss fight with THE JAR (3 stars, 44,620, 448 olives popped, best combo x86), then reached wave 2 of 10 on level 3, The Sink, at about 541 s.
control_trouble: Occasionally my tap for the build panel landed late, and once or twice the flame tap hit a tower instead of the burner underneath. Otherwise tapping a plate and a tile is easy with a finger.
best_moment: Hitting FLAME as a long line of olives crossed the burner and the combo counter shot to x65 with coins flooding in.
worst_moment: The first minute of each level is slow, with only a few coins trickling in, and the Jar boss crawls for about two minutes.
verdict: This is the kind of game I actually play on the bus. I understood it in seconds: put sandwiches on plates, press start, olives die with satisfying splats and a combo counter. I always had something to spend crumbs on, stars at the end, and a new kitchen every few minutes with a new trick (burners, then the sink). It looks like a real product and it never confused me. Nothing hard to read, no walking around. I would keep it and come back this week.
